The Architect ruled option (a): ToolDeps gains session_fn + audit_as_session_fn, server.cpp wires them, writer_identity resolves the session once (session + effective role), updated_by = session.username, every domain row goes through the bound writer. summary: The unknown-argument key was capped with a byte-wise resize(64) after log_token, splitting a multibyte character so error.message carried invalid UTF-8 (security-guardian SG-1, cpp-safety CS-2, cpp-expert CX-1 independently; reproduced by cpp-expert). Fixed in f1cc14c91: cap first (substr(0,64)) then log_token; tests cover every interior cut of 2/3/4-byte characters.
classification_rationale: the message was documented as always valid text

summary: The parked-writer test joined a std::thread by hand on two explicit paths; a throwing REQUIRE would terminate. Ruled once by the Architect: a hand join in new test code is NOT the manual-cleanup floor (the identical shape ships in test_dex_score_policy_writer.cpp), but fixed anyway with yuzu::test::ScopeExit (release gate, then join) and an exception-unwind section in f1cc14c91.
classification_rationale: hygiene in test code; no production behaviour

summary: The reset approval ticket gates the MCP tool, not the capability: the same supervised token can DELETE over REST with Infrastructure:Write alone, and set can store any valid document (architect ARCH-1, compliance-officer CO-4, consistency-auditor CA-8, security-guardian SG-3). classification_rationale: owner decision not previously recorded where an auditor would find it

summary: Spent-ticket honesty cluster (CA-1, CA-2, UP-1, UP-2, UP-3, UP-5, UP-16, ER-7, DW-8): the reset description over-claimed that a missing if_match spends the ticket (the input schema refuses it first); retryable post-approval errors carry retry_after_ms although repeating the call with the spent approval_id is refused; the handler's own perm_fn 403 carries no recovery text; an unauthorised principal can spend a human approval (the generic gate mints before the per-tool RBAC check). summary: Each set/dry_run writes up to ~220 KB per attempted/success/validate row and two rows per real set; AuditStore::log has no detail cap and retention is 365 days; the per-IP limiter is the only brake (sre SRE-2, unhappy-path UP-17). REST PUT ?dry_run has the same exposure, so this PR adds a client not a path. Core change: filed for follow-up (audit-detail size cap, #6619).

ADR-1005 residuals lacked numbers/dates and the 2026-11-06 entry still said its rows flip when the twins land (enterprise-readiness ER-5, compliance-officer CO-5, docs-writer DW-4/DW-5, architect ARCH-2/ARCH-3/ARCH-8). Fixed across f1cc14c91 and 85b49fd25: dated note under the 2026-11-06 entry, a consolidated 'Owner decisions pending ADR-owner acceptance' bullet (ticket vs capability; NO_GATE 14 to 16; preview row twinned vs exception; generic row residual) and the follow-ups worded 'to be filed on merge'.

Coverage gaps on correct code (quality-engineer QE-1/2/5, compliance CO-6, happy-path HP-N1, architect ARCH-4, Codex F-codex-1..5): reset's two loud gates had no denial test; audit_persisted:false unasserted on error branches; updated_by/principal unasserted; provider->current() after set/reset; role capture by an elevated non-admin session; reset message translation; exception unwind. All added across f1cc14c91/15e33db40; mutation probe by the engineer confirmed the new tests fail under the reverted behaviours. Remaining NICE: a reset generic-row drop case (QE2-1).
classification_rationale: test strength only; production behaviour correct
